source.title: SDUM: A Scalable Deep Unrolled Model for Universal MRI Reconstruction
source.authors: Puyang Wang; Peng-Fei Guo; Ke-Yi Chai; Jin-Yuan Zhou; Da-Guang Xu; Shan-Shan Jiang

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study runs its own model-size, depth, and data scaling experiments in MRI reconstruction, a different modality and training setting from language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the original language-model scaling-law studies as background, but reports no language-model results. Its own MRI scaling sweeps and architecture comparisons are recorded below. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy, test predictions from small runs on much larger runs, or find a compute-optimal parameter/data allocation.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own depth, width and data-fraction sweeps for an MRI reconstruction model and reports validation PSNR. PSNR is 10·log10(MAX²/MSE), so PSNR rising linearly in log(parameters) means reconstruction MSE falls roughly as a power law. That bears on V5, whether the power-law form holds in other modalities and regimes. It tests no language-model version (V1–V4, V6, V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report PSNR approximately linear in log(parameters) with depth up to T=18 (r=0.986), and diminishing but unsaturated gains from data. They add that depth scales capacity more efficiently than width, which saturates after about 42M. They say compute-optimal trade-offs are not fully characterized, and recommend diversity-aware data scaling and compute-efficient scaling.
record.recipe_differences: MRI reconstruction rather than language-model pretraining; varies unrolled cascade depth, network width, and data fraction; reports PSNR/SSIM/NMSE rather than held-out cross-entropy. No compute-optimal allocation is estimated.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with backbone and down-sampling depth; width gains saturate after approximately 42M parameters, and data gains diminish at higher data fractions.

fits_no_version.finding: At approximately matched parameter count (T=6), backbone family changes PSNR by up to 3.4 dB (U-Net 28.73 vs Restormer 32.09).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In non-language domains, architecture family at fixed parameter count changes scaling-relevant performance substantially.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-cascade down-sampling depth changes PSNR by about 0.5 dB; one layer fails to train.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-block hierarchical depth affects reconstruction quality in MRI models.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling via unrolled depth gives larger gains than scaling width; 3 cascades beat 1 cascade × 3 iterations at similar compute (Table 3f).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth versus width allocation of parameters affects scaling efficiency in unrolled models.

record.problems: Scaling results use reconstruction metrics rather than held-out loss. The paper reports a depth correlation and R2 but no per-result uncertainty estimates. The scaling analysis is limited to the reported MRI model, depth/data ranges, and evaluation setting; the authors say compute-optimal trade-offs are not fully characterized.

untested.parts: All of it: language-model held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All of it: no extrapolation from small runs to larger ones is tested.
All of it: no compute-optimal parameter/data split; the authors say compute-optimal trade-offs are not characterized.
All of it: no language-model shape-at-fixed-size test. The MRI backbone and down-sampling ablations concern different systems and architecture families.

Scaling over several orders of magnitude (depth spans about 1.3 decades, data 0.4 decades); scaling with compute; any fitted exponent; held-out training loss rather than PSNR; modalities beyond MRI reconstruction.
All of it: no fitting-choice comparison (aside from the width bend noted under V5).

record.verdict_notes: Training objective is SSIM loss; the scaling measure is validation PSNR (log of MSE), so linear PSNR vs log N maps to power-law MSE. Larger depths use progressive warm-started expansion (6→10→18) with about 20k steps per stage, confounding depth with training schedule. Model widths were tuned to fit GPU memory. No uncertainties per scaling point. The reader's V4 links (r1–r8) were removed: they concern MRI backbone and pyramid choices, not LM shape.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, and compute.
Extrapolation from small language-model runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal language-model parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Language-model loss and whether the architecture effect remains slight across a wide range of language-model sizes and settings.
Other modalities and regimes beyond MRI reconstruction; the study measures reconstruction PSNR/SSIM/NMSE, not held-out pretraining loss.
Downstream-task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices, and whether language-model curves bend from power laws.
